nodes.title: PROJECT SETTINGS — shared by every segment
READ FIRST — setup and cloning
widgets_values:
H3 REFERENCE CHAIN

simpleGen fills this template on every run: the agent writes each segment's prompt and the app sets the reference pictures, timing, seeds and segment count. The steps below apply when you open and run the template by hand in ComfyUI.

1. Install the ComfyUI-Minimax-H3-Extender and ComfyUI-H3ReferenceChain node packages (a ComfyUI version with the MiniMax H3 nodes) and the H3 models selected in the loaders.

2. Load your reference pictures into PICTURE 1-4. Picture numbers in a prompt always refer to these.

3. Edit PROJECT SETTINGS once. 0 on a segment's duration/steps means inherit. Duration includes context overlap.

4. Write each segment's complete prompt directly on its card, under the six section headings.

5. Seed modes: fixed repeats a seed; randomize selects a fresh seed each execution; increment/decrement begin at seed and advance on later executions. Sequences reset when settings change or the server restarts. Reports and checkpoint sidecars record actual seeds.

6. To extend: select the last segment card and copy/paste it. Connect PROJECT to project, and the old last card's next_segment to previous. Change the new prompt/seed, then connect its assembled_video to SAVE FINAL. No internal edits or manual segment numbering.

7. Keep upstream seeds fixed when rerolling a later segment. Changes upstream invalidate dependent continuation.

8. Default: three 8-second windows, 22-frame overlap, 24 fps; approximately 22.17 seconds delivered. Actual trimming is reported by the extender.

9. Save individual takes with new_segment_video. Main SAVE FINAL receives assembled_video.

10. Optional extra_reference_5...9 slots accept approved environment views. Define their role in every relevant prompt. Empty slots are skipped.

11. Original references persist. Previous state carries only the last raw clip plus the assembled output separately. No future keyframes are required.

SIZE: Choose width_height for exact dimensions, or megapixels to scale the width:height ratio to a target pixel area. RESOLVED FRAME SIZE shows actual dimensions after rounding to 32.
